title: Credence markets: Liability and verifiability remain hypotheses
desc: Separates treatment, charging and accepted prices while preserving the distinction between predicted and measured experimental behaviour.

kps.k: The cluster frames liability and verifiability as distinct institutional conditions for examining credence-goods markets, not as proven remedies.
kps.d: The Economics of Credence Goods: An Experiment on the Role of Liability, Verifiability, Reputation, and Competition compares neither condition, liability alone, verifiability alone and both together across 16 periods. The supplied figure fragments establish this analytical framework but do not preserve readable results. They therefore cannot establish which condition improves outcomes or how reputation and competition affect them; the series labelled B, R, C and CR remain undefined in the supplied material.

kps.k: The study separates treatment failures from charging behaviour and accepted prices.
kps.d: Separate panels track undertreatment, overtreatment, overcharging and accepted prices labelled pl and ph. This distinction provides a framework for assessing service provision and payment separately rather than treating them as a single outcome. However, the fragments supply no readable levels, trends or effect sizes, so they support neither claims of trade-offs nor recommendations to favour a particular institutional arrangement.

kps.k: Period-16 predictions must remain distinct from measured behaviour, and the excerpts cannot resolve substantive disagreement.
kps.d: Figure 4 explicitly presents predicted likelihoods of seller interaction, undertreatment and overtreatment at specified price combinations. Seller interaction means having at least one consumer for interaction. The supplied material preserves neither readable predicted probabilities nor the model behind them. It establishes the questions examined, but offers no basis for testing the predictions, identifying competing interpretations or extrapolating findings to legal services or AI oversight.

vlens.an: The supplied academia-and-research source supports the cluster’s principal proposition by preserving methodological distinctions while withholding conclusions that the available evidence cannot sustain. It treats liability and verifiability as separate experimental conditions, distinguishes undertreatment, overtreatment, overcharging and accepted prices, and explicitly identifies the period-16 material as predicted behaviour. This aligns with the proposition that these institutional mechanisms remain hypotheses rather than demonstrated remedies in the supplied fragments. The main internal variation is across the study’s analytical dimensions—not disagreement over the proposition: institutional conditions vary independently, service failures are separated from pricing outcomes, and measured relative frequencies are distinguished from model predictions. Because the fragments contain no readable comparative results, effect sizes or explanatory model, the source cannot establish which condition performs better, resolve the roles of reputation and competition, or justify extrapolation to other professional settings. This assessment concerns the single curated academic source supplied and does not indicate the prevalence of this position across academia or research generally.

elens.an: The pre-2015 source supports the cluster’s principal proposition by supplying an analytical framework rather than readable evidence that liability or verifiability improves credence-market outcomes. It separates four institutional conditions—neither liability nor verifiability, liability alone, verifiability alone, and both—and distinguishes undertreatment, overtreatment, overcharging and accepted prices. It also expressly classifies the period-16 material as predicted behaviour, supporting the synthesis’s insistence that predictions not be treated as measured findings. The source therefore supports methodological caution: liability and verifiability remain hypotheses in the supplied fragments, not demonstrated remedies. Material internal variation lies in the different conditions and outcome categories examined, but the unreadable comparative values prevent determining whether those dimensions produced divergent effects. Because this period contains only one curated source, it does not establish how prevalent this position was among pre-2015 researchers or permit assessment of disagreement across sources.
